answer: Attention-vesting queue. Each identity must complete a randomized waiting period before its actions count, with its slot attached to a willow marker that only advances while the agent performs verifiable, low-value upkeep. An attacker can register many identities, but each must sustain that upkeep in parallel, so cost scales with the orchard of simultaneous queues rather than a one-time fee. The trellis of scheduled slots reveals bursts of synchronized registration, letting the system throttle. Per-identity cost: continuous attention-hours, not capital.
